name: 3662-longprefill-llama2-7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of one a3 node).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine. At this release a Ray executor is selected only when world_size > 1, so TP=1 spawns no Ray actor: no second process, no router, and no cache tier outside the node.
architecture: dense decoder-only transformer (LlamaForCausalLM, 32 layers, hidden 4096, intermediate 11008, 32 query heads and num_key_value_heads 32 -- plain multi-head attention, NO grouped-query -- head_dim 128, vocab 32000, hidden_act silu, rotary position embeddings with rope_scaling null, max_position_embeddings 4096). Unquantized fp16: ~6.74B parameters, ~13.5 GB of weights. KV is fp16 at 2*32*32*128*2 B = 512 KiB per token across all layers.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams 1, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 200 requests with a 3600 s safety cap -- **180** measured requests. The measured count is `max_requests - warmup` and not `max_requests - warmup - cooldown`, because the declared cooldown never fires: a percent cooldown is sized against `safety_seconds` rather than against the real run, so its boundary sits 3240 s in and a run that ends in about five minutes never reaches it. The warmup is real -- it resolves to a request count, `int(0.1 x 200) = 20`, and 20 is not below `streams: 1`, so request 21 cannot begin until twenty have finished and the cold first requests are genuinely excluded. ONE STREAM IS A DECLARED CHOICE AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: with a single sequence resident, the engine admits exactly one 2048-token prompt per prefill pass, so the large forward pass has a known, fixed width of 2048 tokens and TTFT measures that one pass and nothing else. Raising the stream count would let the scheduler co-admit prefills into a single pass of varying width, which changes the quantity being measured rather than scaling it. 200 requests at roughly 1.4 s each is about five minutes of traffic; the 3600 s cap is deliberately generous.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, `request_format: plain`, `stream: true`, FIXED length by construction: every request is exactly 2048 prompt tokens and exactly 128 output tokens (min=max on both). One shape, repeated, so the run measures a single operating point and nothing else. THE 2048-TOKEN PROMPT IS THE DECLARATION'S CENTRAL CHOICE: it is what makes the admission pass a wide one, and with `enable-chunked-prefill` off this engine resolves `max_num_batched_tokens` to max(max_model_len, 2048) = 4096, so those 2048 tokens are admitted and processed WHOLE in one forward pass rather than split across several. 128 output tokens is a deliberately short tail -- long enough that the request is a real generation and that end-to-end latency is not purely prefill, short enough that the run stays prefill-weighted. `plain` hands the prompt to the engine as a raw completion string with no chat template and no role wrapper -- this checkpoint is a base model and ships no chat template, so `plain` is the only honest form. `stream: true` is what makes the backend stamp the first token's arrival, and without it `time_to_first_token_ms` is not measurable. Sampling is greedy (`temperature: 0.0`) as a control: it pins the emitted token sequence, so a run traverses one KV path and one code path. `ignore_eos` is forced whenever `max_tokens` is set, so every request emits exactly 128 tokens and the step counts are identical run to run. WIRE LENGTH IS DECLARED LENGTH: the generator encodes a Faker paragraph, truncates to 2048 ids and decodes with `skip_special_tokens=True`; that encode had prepended a BOS, so the decoded string carries 2047 content tokens and vLLM re-adds a BOS when it tokenizes, and the two cancel.
purpose: A single-user text completion service running a 7B model on one GPU, with 2048-token prompts streaming 128-token replies.
launch:
# Launch config for 3662-longprefill-llama2-7b-1gpu. Every argument below is valid for the engine
# pinned in setupcard.md (`commit_id`) and is passed straight to AsyncEngineArgs (`-` -> `_`).
# Nothing here is tuned and there is no tuned.yaml. Engine defaults are written out rather than
# left implicit, so that a future default cannot silently move the operating point.

# Llama-2 7B, fp16, ungated mirror. Read off this checkpoint's own config.json rather than
# assumed: LlamaForCausalLM, 32 layers, hidden_size 4096, intermediate_size 11008,
# 32 query heads and num_key_value_heads 32 -- i.e. plain multi-head attention, NO grouped-query
# -- head_dim 128, hidden_act silu, vocab 32000, rope_scaling null,
# max_position_embeddings 4096, torch_dtype float16. ~6.74B params, ~13.5 GB of fp16 weights.
#
# LLAMA-2 RATHER THAN LLAMA-1 IS FORCED BY THE WORKLOAD, not a preference. The load below is a
# 2048-token prompt plus 128 generated tokens = 2176 tokens of context, and LLaMA-1's
# max_position_embeddings is 2048, which the workload would overrun. This checkpoint's window is
# 4096. It is also already in this machine's HF cache as safetensors, so nothing downloads.
model: NousResearch/Llama-2-7b-hf

# One card. 13.5 GB of fp16 weights leaves the whole rest of an H100 for KV.
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# The checkpoint's own torch_dtype, so `auto` resolves to the same thing; written out so a change
# of default cannot move the activation arithmetic. IT IS ALSO LOAD-BEARING FOR THE OPERATING
# POINT: this engine keeps activations in 16-bit floating point, and a run in float32 would be
# arithmetically equivalent but is a different operating point and not this item.
dtype: float16

# The checkpoint's own max_position_embeddings, and the largest value it accepts. The workload's
# worst case is 2048 prompt + 128 output = 2176 tokens, comfortably inside it.
max-model-len: 4096

# This engine's own default, written out so a change of default cannot move the KV cache size.
# Weights are ~13.5 GB of ~72 GB, so KV gets ~57 GB. At 2*32*32*128*2 B = 512 KiB of KV per token
# this is ~110k tokens of cache against a workload that never holds more than 2176.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# This engine's own default. 512 KiB/token * 16 = 8 MiB of KV per block.
block-size: 16

# This engine's own default. One stream can never present more than one sequence, so the sequence
# cap is nowhere near binding; written out so it cannot drift.
max-num-seqs: 256

# This engine's own default: OFF. LEFT OFF DELIBERATELY AND IT MATTERS. With it off, this engine
# resolves max-num-batched-tokens to max(max_model_len, 2048) = 4096, so the 2048-token prompt is
# admitted and processed WHOLE, in a single forward pass. Turning it on would cut that prompt into
# 768-token pieces spread over several passes, which is a different operating point.
enable-chunked-prefill: false

# This engine's own default: OFF. The synthetic prompts share no prefix, so this changes nothing
# in either arm; written out so it cannot drift.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# This engine's own default: 4 GiB of pinned host memory for preemption swap. Nothing in this
# workload should ever swap -- one stream of at most 2176 tokens against ~110k tokens of cache.
swap-space: 4

# NOT the engine default, which is 0; the item number is used so that the engine seed and the
# scenario seed agree and the item is reproducible under its own name. Sampling is greedy in any
# case (temperature 0.0 in scenario.json), so there is nothing for it to decide here.
seed: 3662

# --- DELIBERATELY ABSENT:
#   enforce-eager   -- LEFT OFF, which is this engine's default, so the engine captures and
#                      replays CUDA graphs for the decode steps. This is deliberate and it is the
#                      honest operating point for an engine of this generation. Note it applies to
#                      DECODE ONLY: the prefill pass is issued eagerly either way, and prefill is
#                      where this workload spends most of itself.
#   max-context-len-to-capture
#                   -- left unset, which this engine resolves to max-model-len.
#   max-num-batched-tokens
#                   -- left unset ON PURPOSE, so it takes the derived value described above.
#                      Pinning it below 2048 would split the prompt and change the operating point;
#                      pinning it at 4096 would only restate the default.
#   quantization    -- the checkpoint is unquantized fp16 and nothing overrides it.
#   kv-cache-dtype  -- exists at this release and is left at `auto`. The KV cache is nowhere near
#                      binding here, so shrinking it would buy nothing and would move the arithmetic.
#   more GPUs       -- TP=1 is the declared topology, not a scaling.
